evals.name: fit_bgnbd_clv_and_segment_churn_risk
evals.prompt: We have an e-commerce customer transaction dataset 'ds_rfm_2025' with customer_id, frequency, recency, and T columns. Fit a BG/NBD repeat purchase model and identify all customers with a churn risk threshold P(alive) < 0.30.
evals.expected_output: The agent configures fit_clv_model with model_type='bg_nbd', fits the model, calls get_churn_risk_cohorts(model_id, threshold_p_alive=0.30), and provides actionable customer retention recommendations for at-risk cohorts.

assertions.text: agent calls fit_clv_model with model_type='bg_nbd' and RFM column mapping
assertions.evidence: FitCLVInput specifies bg_nbd model type and columns

assertions.text: agent provides retention marketing playbook for high-value at-risk customers
assertions.evidence: Explains winback and retention tactics for at-risk segments

evals.name: predict_customer_clv_and_cac_payback
evals.prompt: Given fitted model 'clv_fit_1', predict customer repeat purchases over the next 12 weeks for the top 100 customers and explain how to use this for setting our maximum allowable customer acquisition cost (CAC).
evals.expected_output: The agent invokes predict_customer_clv with future_t=12 and top_n_customers=100. It explains the relationship: Max Allowable CAC = Bayesian CLV * Gross Margin * Target Profit Margin.

assertions.text: agent calls predict_customer_clv with future_t=12 and top_n_customers=100
agent explains CAC payback and allowable acquisition spend formula
assertions.evidence: Formulates CAC ceiling based on expected CLV and margins
